Every man is just a version of the funniest woman he knows. So, the lady in this video said that women are way funnier than men and that every man is just a version of the funniest woman he knows. That's a bold claim, but it got me thinking. Is there actually research on who is funnier, men or women? And how would you even measure that? Can you actually put someone's sense of humor on a scale? Well, turns out, researchers have tried. The most common method is pretty simple. You give people a picture or a weird prompt and ask them to write something funny. Then a group of judges rates the answers without knowing who wrote them. No names, no faces, no gender. Just a joke. In 2020, psychologists Gil Greengross, Paul Sylvia, and Emily Nussbaum collected 28 of these studies spanning over 40 years and more than 5,000 participants, two-thirds of them women. They combined everything into one meta-analysis, basically a study of studies. The result? Men's jokes were rated funnier on average. Now, before anyone starts celebrating, the difference was small. If you pick a random man and a random woman, the man writes the funnier caption about 6 times out of 10, which means 4 times out of 10, she wins. A slight edge. Nowhere near a comedy monopoly. And the lead author himself said the study often gets misread as women aren't funny, which is not what they found. So the claim from the video doesn't really hold up, but neither does the old stereotype that women aren't funny. There's also a smaller study from 2012 at UC San Diego. It also rated men's captions slightly funnier. But then people were shown funny and unfunny captions, told whether a man or a woman wrote each one, and later tested on who wrote what. When they got it wrong, they leaned toward giving the unfunny captions to women and the funny ones to men. And when guessing on captions they'd never seen, they credited the funny ones to men more often. But same caveat as before, small effect. And only 72 students. But it suggests the old stereotype might get a little extra help from memory on top of the real difference. So why is there a gap at all? One idea comes from dating. A 2006 study found that women tend to value a partner who makes them laugh, while men value a partner who laughs at their jokes. So men may simply have more incentive to be funny. And as a result, they could be practicing it more. But researchers still debate whether the gap comes from evolution, social expectations, or both. It's also worth saying this study mostly measured one type of humor, quick written wit on command. Storytelling, sarcasm among friends, timing in a real conversation, all of that is much harder to put in a lab. So who is funnier, men or women? On one narrow test, men by a small margin. In real life, it depends a lot more on the person than on the gender. And if the line, every man is a version of the funniest woman he knows, did make you laugh, don't worry. According to that 2012 study, people will just assume a woman wrote it.
